decision.title: The book's XQuery and XSD parts (packet book-2)

body.p: , after . The owner asked the book to cover XQuery and XSD as deeply as XPath and XSLT, so that a reader who knows neither can learn them and work with sxml from the book alone.

item.p: Structure. Chapter 3 (XQuery) has eleven sections: FLWOR, Grouping and Windows, Building XML, Conditions/Types/Errors, Functions and Modules, Documents/Parameters/Context, Writing Results, Updating Documents, What's New in XQuery 4.0, and a project chapter (a loans report: one library module, HTML, JSON and fn:put outputs; examples in docs/book/examples/xquery-project). Chapter 5 (XSD) has nine: the introduction, Simple Types and Facets, Complex Types and Content Models, Deriving Types, Namespaces and Larger Schemas, Keys and References, XSD 1.1 Features, Reading Validation Errors, Typed Data and Schema-Aware Queries. Top-level chapter numbers are unchanged, so "Chapter N" references elsewhere still hold. Full Text stays in Chapter 7; the XQuery part points there.

Only what works. Every feature shown was run against a release build; what the CLI lacks is said plainly: no fn:collection (the book shows --param lists and file:list instead), no xsi:schemaLocation following, no fn:trace/fn:message output in sxml xquery.

Findings for later packets (QUEUE, not fixed here: the book avoids them): collection("relative") in sxml xquery/xpath ends with exit 4 and expression: SXML_STATUS_INVALID_ARGUMENT instead of err:FODC0002 (an absolute URI gives FODC0002); a dynamic error raised in a library module is reported with the main module's file name and the library module's line and column ($err:module is right); xsi:type="xs:string" resolves the prefix xs in an instance that does not declare it (cvc-elt.4.1 expected); sxml xpath and sxml xquery install no trace sink, so fn:trace and fn:message write nothing; after an element that cvc-complex-type.2.4 rejects, the rest of its parent's content is not assessed (recovery, not a wrong verdict); the CLI's --context-item document has no document-uri.
Verified: tools/check-book-examples.sh on a release build of a HEAD snapshot, for every chapter file the packet touched.
